game: MIA@CAR Week 5 2025, kickoff 2025-10-05 13:00 ET, CAR +1.5, total 44.5, outdoors

script.base: A close, run-lean game. MIA is only -1.5 with implied totals MIA 23.0 and CAR 21.5 on a 44.5 total, so the book is not pricing a blowout or a shootout. Both run defenses allow 5.23-5.25 YPC, CAR blitzes just 23%, and CAR is not a 3.5+ dog, so both teams can stay on schedule on the ground: Achane as the late hammer if MIA leads, Dowdle as the Hubbard replacement in a balanced CAR script.
script.flip1: MIA scores first and CAR chases. MIA blitzes 40% and Bryce Young is at -0.30 EPA/db when blitzed versus +0.03 when not, so CAR abandons the run, Dowdle's carries die, and short throws go to Tremble, Renfrow and Hubbard's old targets instead of rush yards.
script.flip2: CAR's front (5.23 YPC, Wharton out) cannot stop Achane, MIA grinds the clock, and Hill/Waddle air yards stall the way a favorite-runs script stalls QB and WR production. A true shootout is the other miss: both rush shares get squeezed by pass volume.

injury_fallout: Source: nflverse official injury report, pre-game, not the 90-minute inactive list. CAR RB Chuba Hubbard Out (calf) is the usage flip: he had 37 carries and 160 yards in weeks 2-4, so the next man is Rico Dowdle (25/71 in that same window, rush yards by week 12, 9, 30, 32) with Trevor Etienne (7/33; rush yards 4, 0, 33) the committee risk, not the lead. CAR TE Ja'Tavion Sanders Out (ankle) pushes TE targets toward Tommy Tremble (13 targets, 78 yards in weeks 2-4). CAR DT Tershawn Wharton Out (toe), with DT Cam Jackson, DE LaBryan Ray and LB D.J. Wonnum only Questionable, softens the interior Achane runs at; those Q tags are not treated as out. CAR CB Chau Smith-Wade Out (chest) is a coverage loss for Hill/Waddle, but shell and alignment are not charted. MIA WR Cedrick Wilson Jr. Out (knee) is a small bump for Malik Washington, not a primary-target change. MIA CB Storm Duck Out (ankle) is a coverage loss for McMillan/Renfrow, uncharted as to side.

matchup.shell: No coverage charting, MOFO/MOFC or man/zone rate in the pack. Proxy only: CAR blitz rate 23% so MIA should see mostly unhurried base looks; MIA blitz rate 40%.
matchup.pressure: Tua is the one who wants CAR's low blitz: MIA EPA/db is -0.34 when blitzed and +0.19 when not. Young is the one hurt by pressure: CAR EPA/db is -0.30 when blitzed and +0.03 when not. MIA's 40% blitz is the CAR-run killer if it creates obvious passing downs; it also funnels checkdowns, which is a TE/RB receiving note, not the market being used.
matchup.bleeds: CAR run defense: 5.23 YPC and 13 runs of 10+ in four games; pass location YPA middle 9.5 (28), left 7.06 (47), right 4.98 (41); 11 passes of 20+ for 118 yards. MIA run defense: 5.25 YPC and 20 runs of 10+; pass location YPA right 9.68 (41), left 8.27 (44), middle 7.41 (22); 10 passes of 20+ for 115 yards.
matchup.overlap: The clean overlap is run, not a charted WR-versus-shell overlap. Achane (43 carries, 191 rush yards in weeks 2-4) runs into the CAR front that allows 5.23 YPC with Wharton out. Dowdle, once Hubbard's carries are vacant, runs into the MIA front that allows 5.25 YPC and 20 explosive runs. Hill is the MIA target leader (23 targets, 313 air yards, 225 yards in three games) and McMillan is CAR's (26 targets, 266 air yards, 210 yards), but without alignment data their overlap with middle/right YPA bleeds is unproven, and MIA's blitz works against McMillan's deep yards.

form: Windows are weeks 2-4 plus the listed last-4, which lines up as week 1 then weeks 2-4 (Achane rush 55+30+62+99 and L3 30+62+99=191; Dowdle 12+9+30+32 and L3 9+30+32=71). Achane rush trend is 55, 30, 62, 99, so the last two games cleared 58.5, with a week-2 script where the yards showed up in receiving (92) instead of rushing (30). Hill last-4 receiving 40, 109, 49, 67 sits on the 58.5 line despite a 75-yard L3 average inflated by the 109. Waddle 30, 68, 39, 48 sits on 43.5. McMillan 68, 100, 48, 62 sits on 65.5. Dowdle is the role change: rush yards 12, 9, 30, 32 while still the complement to Hubbard, YPC only 2.84 on 25 carries (71 yards), so efficiency is ordinary and the edge is carries, not a hot average. Etienne 4, 0, 33 is a one-play profile. Tremble 2, 20, 16, 42 is too spiky to be a second leg. No similar-defense or coverage-chart sample is in the pack.

pre_mortem: It is Monday and both rush overs lost because the Hubbard news was already in the 21.5 and the backfield was a committee: Etienne's 33-yard game type stole the vacated carries, Dowdle stayed on 8-10 inefficient touches, and MIA's 40% blitz put Young in a hole by the second quarter so CAR never had a run script. Achane lost the other way: CAR dared Tua to throw, Gordon vultured the grind carries, and Achane posted another 30-rush / 90-receiving line that misses 58.5 rush yards while the rush-plus-rec line would have been the one that cashed. A late inactive or a snap limit on either back, neither of which is known yet, would do the same thing. That counter-case is real on price confirmation, which is why Dowdle is flagged rather than sized, but it is not stronger than the usage read while 21.5 still looks like the complement number.
slip_story: One story only: close game, both bad run defenses, moderate 44.5 total, Hubbard out, Wharton out. Stack is Dowdle rush yards over with Achane rush yards over. Do not add Hill, Waddle or McMillan overs; those need the pass-volume flip. Do not add a total under as a same-slip requirement. No TD legs. Etienne over 4.5 is the same story but a lower-share dart, left off.
